user_saw: Agent Git content commands (show, diff, log, restore) naming a missing commit in a shared blobless clone triggered Git lazy fetches that downloaded about a million objects and took seconds.
summary: The agent Git PATH shim now prepares missing revision roots with negotiated blobless fetches before content commands and stops instead of falling back to Git's full-history lazy fetch.
reasoning: The expensive transfer is Git's own promisor lazy-fetch behavior (noop negotiation), which existed before OpenClaw's agent Git shim; the shim was added two days earlier (b6d8eb287e0, #195498) for probes, and this change extends its mitigation to content commands. Nothing ever made these commands cheaper and then broke it, so this is a performance extension rather than a defect origin.
